searchText: Does this actually mean anything? https://twitter.com/CryptoBlkChnTec/status/1329266057538899969?s=20 Somewhat related to above, what do people generally use to monitor the health of the chain? I'd really like to set up a grafana dashboard to keep an eye on things like txs per block, average gas price, storage slots written / read, new accounts, etc. Geth has the `--metric` flag to enable collection of a lot of those metrics and you can easily add more to the code. Docs for that can be found here: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/22030 These metrics can be written into an influxdb to be read by grafana. We might be able to share our grafana config for displaying the most useful/important metrics. <@360491619402776577> that's awesome there are some docs now, I'll finally be able to stop reading the geth 1.9.0 release blog post 🙂 I have a grafana dashboard setup for those metrics, but they generally seem to be "geth client metrics" whereas I'm also interested in "ethereum mainnet metrics". I could definitely add more metrics to the code, but if I'm going to do some work to make these stats easily accessible I'd prefer to do it in a way that others can use it. Do you think there is a desire to merge additional metrics into geth upstream that expose more mainnet information? Maybe even under a different flag? If not, it may make more sense to write a light service that queries the client's rpc and submits the data to influxdb/prometheus - unfortunately some things like new accounts created aren't readily available from rpc I think they roll off tomorrow https://etherscan.io/block/countdown/11519999 Actually in 8 hours <@403426778401734657> why that block? Dag size is grows to 4 gigs <@403426778401734657> https://etherscan.io/block/countdown/11519999 Can you elaborate little about this For what the countdown is ? As the Dag size grows (a part of the mining algorithm) miners with memory below the Dag size are no longer able to keep the Dag in memory Meaning any GPU or ASIC with less memory than the Dag size is unable to mine Ethereum. The Dag size grows each block in a predictable manner That’s the block when the Dag size reaches 4gb

excerpts.content: Somewhat related to above, what do people generally use to monitor the health of the chain? I'd really like to set up a grafana dashboard to keep an eye on things like txs per block, average gas price, storage slots written / read, new accounts, etc.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
Geth has the `--metric` flag to enable collection of a lot of those metrics and you can easily add more to the code.
Docs for that can be found here: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/22030
These metrics can be written into an influxdb to be read by grafana.
We might be able to share our grafana config for displaying the most useful/important metrics.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: <@360491619402776577> that's awesome there are some docs now, I'll finally be able to stop reading the geth 1.9.0 release blog post 🙂 I have a grafana dashboard setup for those metrics, but they generally seem to be "geth client metrics" whereas I'm also interested in "ethereum mainnet metrics". I could definitely add more metrics to the code, but if I'm going to do some work to make these stats easily accessible I'd prefer to do it in a way that others can use it. Do you think there is a desire to merge additional metrics into geth upstream that expose more mainnet information? Maybe even under a different flag? If not, it may make more sense to write a light service that queries the client's rpc and submits the data to influxdb/prometheus - unfortunately some things like new accounts created aren't readily available from rpc
